description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, b2-26: a log parser's month table `my %mon = do { my $i = 0; map { $_ => ++$i } qw(Jan Feb ...) }` made every month 12).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.
REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/preinc1.pl + .perl.out / .pcl.out -- ten rows, ONLY row 1 differs):
  my $i = 0; my %m = map { $_ => ++$i } qw(a b c);        perl a=1,b=2,c=3      PCL a=3,b=3,c=3
RIGHT on both: `map { $_ => $j++ }` (post-increment yields a copy), `map { ++$k } 1..3` (a ONE-element result), `push @q, ++$p for 1..3`, `map { $t += 2 } 1..3`, `map { [++$v] } ...`, `$y{$_} = ++$x for ...`, and `my @s = (++$r, ++$r)` = "2 2" on BOTH (perl's own alias quirk: pre-increment returns the variable itself -- PCL reproduces it faithfully, which is the point: the block's list holds the BOX).
perl's rule: `map` COPIES each value its block returns when it is not a temporary (pp_mapwhile: "copy the values unless they are TEMPs"), once per iteration, so the alias never survives the iteration.  PCL copies for a one-element result and NOT for a multi-element one -- find the two collection paths in the runtime's `p-map` (or in the emitted lambda's result handling) and make the multi-value path unbox/copy exactly as the single-value path does (rule 11: one collector).  Probe the family: `grep` returns ALIASES (must NOT copy: `$_++ for grep { 1 } @a` modifies @a -- keep), `sort` likewise returns aliases, `map { ($_, ++$i) }`, `map { +{ k => ++$i } }`, `map { $i += 1; ($_, $i) }` (returns the box of $i twice?), a compound-assign result `map { $_ => ($n .= "x") }`, and the EXPR form `map +($_ => ++$i), LIST`.
BAR: `cl/` runtime (or emission, if the copy belongs in the lambda) => full sweep + companion op/grep.t op/list.t op/inc.t legs; bench control `map`-heavy rows (a per-element copy on the multi-value path only; FLAG > 2 %); guard rows in an existing map/grep Pl/t file, INVERSE-verified.


=== DONE (s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
SHIPPED in commit "#2005: map COPIES what its block returns, on EVERY result arity".

THE TWO PATHS: `p-map` had two collection arms -- the single-element arm copied the value
(%p-map-copy-scalar), the multi-element arm pushed the block's own boxes, so a result list carrying
a variable's box stored that box once per key and every one of them read the final value.  ONE
COLLECTOR now (rule 11): the multi-element arm copies through the same helper.  perl's pp_mapwhile
copies the values unless they are TEMPs, once per iteration, so the alias never survives the
iteration.

THE NEGATIVES HOLD: `grep` and `sort` keep returning ALIASES (`$_++ for grep { 1 } @a` writes
through to @a), and `map` still aliases `$_` to the element it reads (`map { $_ *= 2 } @d` modifies
@d).

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3: preinc1 (10 rows) and a 15-row family probe (scratch/s492b/mapfam.pl)
covering `map { ($_, ++$i) }`, `map { +{ k => ++$i } }`, a compound-assign result, the EXPR form
`map +(...), LIST`, nested `map { @$_ }`, `map { %$_ }`, empty and undef results, and the
grep/sort/`$_` negatives -- all identical now; the base was wrong on five.

FLAGGED (the USER's standing rule on a bugfix that slows execution): the multi-element arm now pays
one %p-map-copy-scalar per element.  Measured on a synthetic worst case (`map { ($_, $_ * 2) } 1..200`
as the whole hot loop, best-of-5, startup subtracted, load < 1): +20.8 %.  No bench-exec row has a
map in its hot loop, so the suite is unaffected; the cost is inherent -- the single-element arm has
always paid it, and perl copies too.
NORMATIVE: docs/ir-spec.md 10-map.
GUARD: four rows in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t (132 -> 136); the two positives fail on a 5ce155cb
extraction, the two negatives pass there.
subject: SILENT WRONG (everyday, pre-existing): `map { $_ => ++$i } LIST` stores the FINAL value of $i for every key -- `my %idx = map { $_ => ++$i } qw(a b c)` is a=3,b=3,c=3 (perl a=1,b=2,c=3): the block's multi-element result list carries the variable's BOX and map does not copy it per iteration
